description: On a `tg --tag decision …` send, runs the decision-request-discipline self-check: parses (shlex, not raw-match) the message body and, if it is missing structural markers (Context / Options / Recommendation), emits an exit-0 ADVISORY naming what's absent. ADVISORY ONLY — never blocks; a malformed decision request must stay sendable. on_error=open: a formatting reminder, not a boundary. There is NO self-service silence (the old ALLOW_RAW_DECISION_REQUEST env and `# decision-request-ok:` sentinel are removed); a one-time silence is an external Telegram approval requested via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_DECISION_REQUEST_FORMAT="<why>" (deny-by-default; only exit 0 silences). timeout_ms 960000 exceeds the hatch helper's 930s worst case (tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus a 30s cleanup margin) so the requested silence can actually reach a human before the bridge's descriptor-timeout kill; a kill would merely SHOW the advisory (this hook never blocks), but the short 3s default made the silence path un-answerable. Claude Code settings entries that launch cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s. The common env-unset path returns immediately (no tg call, no latency cost).
